label: Sports Clubs
rubric: Depth of heritage identity · Trophy history · Global recognition · Fan devotion

entries.name: FC Barcelona
entries.rationale: 'Més que un club' — a symbol of Catalan identity and culture through decades of Spanish politics.

entries.name: Boca Juniors
entries.rationale: Born of Italian dockworker immigrants in La Boca, Buenos Aires, and still the voice of that neighborhood.

entries.name: Boston Celtics
entries.rationale: Named for the city's Irish-American heritage, now backed by the most championships in NBA history.

entries.name: Celtic FC
entries.rationale: Founded to support Glasgow's Irish Catholic immigrant community, one half of world football's fiercest rivalry.

entries.name: Māori All Blacks
entries.rationale: New Zealand's dedicated Māori rugby side, carrying the haka and indigenous heritage onto the world stage.

entries.name: River Plate
entries.rationale: Founded by English immigrants and Buenos Aires's early elite, earning the nickname 'Los Millonarios'.

entries.name: Rangers FC
entries.rationale: Rooted in Glasgow's Scottish Protestant and Unionist heritage, the other half of the storied Old Firm rivalry.

entries.name: Green Bay Packers
entries.rationale: A small meatpacking town's team, still community-owned in defiance of modern franchise economics.

entries.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
entries.rationale: Named for the steel industry that built the city and its generations of working-class fans.

entries.name: Athletic Bilbao
entries.rationale: Fields only Basque-formed players by policy, a unique stand for regional identity in elite football.

entries.name: SL Benfica
entries.rationale: Grew out of working-class Lisbon and remains the club of Portugal's largest fan base by far.

entries.name: Galatasaray
entries.rationale: Named for an old Ottoman palace school, carrying Istanbul's imperial heritage into modern football.

entries.name: Notre Dame Fighting Irish
entries.rationale: A Catholic university's team whose Irish nickname became shorthand for American college football itself.

entries.name: Fenerbahçe
entries.rationale: One of Istanbul's great clubs, deeply tied to Anatolian and republican Turkish identity.

entries.name: Olympique de Marseille
entries.rationale: Reflects the Mediterranean port city's fiercely multicultural, working-class character.

entries.name: AS Roma
entries.rationale: Wears the she-wolf of Roman legend and channels the city's ancient civic pride.

entries.name: New Orleans Saints
entries.rationale: Named for the city's Catholic, jazz-funeral heritage and embraced through 'Who Dat' culture.

entries.name: Wales National Rugby Team
entries.rationale: Rugby as a pillar of Welsh national identity, sung in at every match by a stadium in full voice.

entries.name: Feyenoord
entries.rationale: The club of Rotterdam's dockworkers, built on a proudly blue-collar, no-nonsense identity.

entries.name: FC Schalke 04
entries.rationale: Born in Germany's Ruhr coal-mining region, still known as the miners' club.

entries.name: Racing Club
entries.rationale: One of Avellaneda's great clubs, carrying the Italian immigrant heritage of Buenos Aires's south side.

entries.name: Munster Rugby
entries.rationale: A single Irish province whose rugby identity feels closer to nationhood than to a mere club.

entries.name: Cardiff City
entries.rationale: The only non-English club ever to win the FA Cup, carrying Welsh pride into English football.

entries.name: Hibernian FC
entries.rationale: Founded by Irish immigrants in Edinburgh, its name taken straight from Ireland's Latin title.

entries.name: Sunderland AFC
entries.rationale: The 'Black Cats' of Wearside, forged in the identity of shipbuilding and coal-mining communities.
